ImageDescription.value:
Grind the following to a fine paste: one onion, one tomato, 2 cloves garlic

Dry roast the following and grind into a fine powder: 4 long dry red chillies, 1" cinnamon, 4 green cardamoms, 1 tsp cumin seeds, 1 tbsp corriander seeds, 1 tbsp fennel seeds, 4 cloves, 1tbsp whole black pepper.

Heat 3 tbsp olive oil and add 1" finely chopped ginger and fry for 10 seconds. Add the paste and fry for 30 minutes on low heat. Stir occassionally. Add the spice powder and stir well. Add 500gm chicken and fry for 5 min. Add 2 cups water and one cubed potato and cook until done. Serve with rice or naan bread.

ObjectName.value: Chicken Curry (490198749)

Categories.value: Chicken curries|Flickr images reviewed by FlickreviewR 2|Methi chicken|Images from Indian Home cooking Flickr group uploaded by Netha Hussain

ImageDescription.value:
This is a quick and easy chicken curry that would suit most tastes.

Ingredients Whole chicken=====================medium size (approx 1.5 kg) (You can also use boneless chicken 1kg / pre-cut chicken pieces. However fresh whole chicken always tastes the best) Onion======================================2 (medium size) Tomato=====================================3 Green Chili==================================2 (optional) Ginger paste=================================1 tsp Garlic paste=================================1 tsp Vinegar=====================================2 tbsp Garam masala (Curry powder)===============================2 tsp Corriander powder===============================2 tsp Cumin powder===============================1 tsp Red Chili powder===============================1/2 tsp Turmeric powder (haldi)===============================1/2 tsp Cloves=======================================8 Cinnamon===================2 inch piece Cardamom=================8 Bay leaf====================3 Dried fenugreek leaves (Kasturi Methi)===============1 tbsp (optional) Vegetable oil================4 tbsp ☺♥

All these ingredients are available at any Indian store (some supermarkets e.g. Tescos also stock ingredients for Indian cooking now)

Method 1. Joint the chicken (cut into medium size pieces) and remove the skin. 2. Make small cuts on the leg and breast pieces and place in a bowl. Add the Ginger & Garlic paste and the vinegar and mix well. Let the mix marinate for 1/2 hour. 3. Puree the tomatoes in a blender and keep aside. 4. Chop the onions roughly and puree in a blender by adding a little water. 5. Chop the green chilies (optional) 6. Heat the oil in a thick bottomed vessel (not a wok) and add the cinnamon, cloves, cardamom and bay leaf. Stir and fry for ~10 seconds. 7. Add the Onion paste + green chili and mix. 8. Fry the onion paste on medium heat for ~10 minutes until it turns dry. Stir occassionally. 9. Add the tomato paste and fry for ~10 minutes while stirring. 10. Once the mix is dry and you can see a slight film of oil, add the Garam masala (curry powder), Corriander powder, Cumin powder, Red chili powder and turmeric powder and mix. Fry for 2 minutes. 11. Add the marinated chicken pieces and salt and fry for 5 min on high heat. 12. Add enough water (~500 ml) to cover the chicken and cook until done. 13. Add the dried fenugreek leaves and stir (can be substituted with a twist of lime juice)

14. Serve with boiled rice / naan.

ObjectName.value: Chicken and andouille sausage jambalaya

Categories.value: Jambalaya|February 2006 photographs|Flickr images reviewed by FlickreviewR 2|Photos in Flickr Explore

ImageDescription.value:
Adapted from this recipe.

2 lbs of chicken, I bought chicken pieces already taken apart and cleaned. 1 lb. andouille sausage 1 large onion, chopped 1 red bell pepper, chopped 4 cloves garlic, minced 4 ribs celery, chopped 2 small cans tomato paste 1 28-oz. can tomatoes (I only used half a can) 1 14.5-oz. can of diced tomatoes with mild green chilies 8 cups chicken stock Creole seasoning blend 

2 teaspoons cayenne, 2 teaspoons black pepper, 1 teaspoon white pepper, 1 teaspoon oregano, 1/2 teapsoon thyme

2 bay leaves Salt to taste 4 cups long-grain white rice, uncooked. I used Uncle Ben's converted.

In a sauté or frying pan, brown the chicken, sprinkling with red peppers, tyme and a bit of salt. Tear or cut the meat into bite-size pieces.

Brown the sliced andouille sausage and pour off fat.

In the pot, sauté the onions, garlic, peppers and celery in oil until onions begin to turn transparent.

In the same pot, while you're sautéing the "trinity", add the tomato paste and let it pincé, meaning to let it brown a little. What we're going for here is an additional depth of flavor by browning the tomato paste a little; the sugar in the tomato paste begins to caramelize, deepening the flavor and color. Keep it moving so that it browns but doesn't burn. Once the vegetables are translucent and the tomato paste achives sort of a red mahogany color, deglaze the pan with the about 2 cups of the stock, scraping the bottom of the pan to mix up any browned bits, and stir until smooth, making sure the sautéed vegetables, paste and stock are combined thoroughly. It should be fairly thick.

Add the Creole seasoning, tomatoes and salt to taste. Cook over low-medium heat for about 10 minutes. Add the meat and/or seafood and cook another 10 minutes.

Add the rest of the stock, check seasonings, and stir in the rice, combining thoroughly. Cook for about 20-25 minutes, or until the rice has absorbed all the liquid and is cooked through. Tturn the heat down to low-medium and let the sauce thicken up a bit, with the pot uncovered, stirring frequently, for about 10 minutes. Stir thoroughly to combine all ingredients. Most of the liquid should be absorbed.

ImageDescription.value: This photo shows a plate of what appears to be a Thai dish called Pad Kra Pao, or Thai basil stir-fry with ground meat. The dish consists of minced meat (likely pork or chicken) stir-fried with Thai holy basil and other vegetables. It's served alongside a mound of white rice topped with a fried egg that has a runny, bright orange-yellow yolk. This is a very popular Thai street food dish, often served exactly this way with the combination of the spicy meat mixture, plain rice, and fried egg creating a balanced meal. The dish is typically seasoned with fish sauce, soy sauce, garlic, and chili peppers, giving it a spicy, savory flavor profile that's characteristic of Thai cuisine.

Categories.value: Taken with Canon EOS 350D|Chicken dishes|Wok|Flickr images reviewed by File Upload Bot (Magnus Manske)|Files with coordinates missing SDC location of creation

ImageDescription.value:
Ginger Chicken!

One of my favorite dinners! We usually make this with beef, but chicken is what we had, so we just went with it. Jonathan made dumplings to go with. yummm. 

   *   1 lb chicken or steak, sliced into narrow strips
   *   2-3 cups of chopped vegetables (we use carrots, red bell pepper, and broccoli)

   * 3/4 cup cornstarch
   * 1/2 cup water
   * 2 eggs
   
   
   * canola oil
   * 2-4 gloves garlic, minced

   * 6 tablespoons soy sauce
   * 8 tablespoons rice vinegar
   * 2 tablespoons sesame oil
   * 1 tablespoon ground ginger
   * 1/2 cup sugar
   * 3 teaspoons crushed red pepper flakes, to taste
   * 3 green onions, chopped

-Cut chicken or steak into narrow strips. -Cut vegetables into strips/chunks.

-Place 3/4 cup cornstarch in a large bowl, mix in 1/2 cup water (it will be kind of hard to stir), Stir until combined. Whisk in two eggs.

-Heat about an inch of oil in a wok

-Add meat to the cornstarch mixture. Add to the wok and fry in small batches.

-In separate bowl, combine soy sauce, sesame oil, rice vinegar, sugar, red pepper flakes, green onions and ginger.

-When the chicken is done cooking, drain all but a teaspoon of oil. Saute garlic cloves.

-Add meat, vegetables, and sauce mixture to the wok. Stir & then simmer for a few minutes until everything is heated through and coated with sauce.

Serve with rice.

ImageDescription.value:
Hankering for a Char Kway Teow, we head to Penang Coffee House. We also ordered the specials of the Hainanese Chicken Rice, and Chai Tow Kueh, stir-fried cubes of radish cake.

Until I revisited my <a href="/photos/avlxyz/19614174/" rel="nofollow">Chai Tow Kueh from 2005</a>, I had totally forgotten about this uh, forgetable version. And it was soggy. The 炒馃条 Char Kway Teow was quite smoky, maybe even a bit too smoky, and the Hainanese Chicken rice was just ok. Even the Ice Kacang wasn't that great with very coarsely shaved ice, and not like fresh powder snow.

Given the average, or maybe slighty above-average, standard of food, and the above-average prices, it's not surprising that the restaurant that used to be packed on a weekday night is now only three quarters full on a Thursday night.

I wonder if the famous curry laksa is still good? The blogosphere are strangely silent...

Categories.value: Flickr images reviewed by FlickreviewR 2|Files from rice tag of Alpha Flickr stream uploaded by Netha Hussain|Kao Gaeng, Springvale|Rice meals in Australia|Thai cuisine in Melbourne

ImageDescription.value:
Heart-shaped Steamed Rice - Kao Gang AUD2 --- We initially wanted to try Pawan Thai across the car park, but it was full, so it was back to the reliable Kao Gang, only to find that they were under new management. Still the food was as good as before. There were 2 other Thai families dining while we were there. I guess that means it is quite authentic!

We all loved the Thai dressing on the deep-fried bream. It was intensely sweet, sour, salty and spicy hot! It was thick and syrupy. Perhaps it could have been a little less salty, but it was still good. So salty, we had to order an extra serve of plain steamed rice so that we could soak up the dressing! :P

The grilled Thai sausages were a bit of an eye-opener. It was filled with sour pork and toasted rice. I think the sausage was fermented, giving it a tangy sour taste.

Kao Gang 22-38 Queens Avenue, Springvale (03) 9540 3199

Categories.value: Yeung Chow fried rice|Flickr images reviewed by FlickreviewR 2|Files from rice tag of Alpha Flickr stream uploaded by Netha Hussain

ImageDescription.value:
Friday lunch with work colleagues and we ordered up a storm of dumplings!

The 红油水饺 chilli oil dumplings hit the spot with a fair whack of heat from the lashings of chilli oil tempered by the sweet soy sauce. The less fire-loving of us wolfed down the plain 饺子 steamed dumplings which were also prety good. The 锅贴 pan-fried dumplings were nice and crisp, but maybe the pastry was a tad thick. We also had a serve of the 炒手拉面 stir-fried handmade noodles which were chewy and smooth. I've always loved the handmade noodles there. Another star was the 菜肉炒饭 special fried rice with bits of 火腿 Chinese ham and crisp vegetables.

We also ordered a couple of gwailo favourites just to see how they fared. Kane thought the 豉汁牛肉 black bean beef was awesome, but Davina and I thought it was gluggy and pretty bland. No one really liked the 柠檬鸡 Lemon Chicken, declaring it "too lemony". I thought it was pretty good, especially since they were very generous with the sauce, even if it was straight out of a bottle. The sauce was probably Chinese-style lemon sauce that's very similar to 酸梅浆 preserved plum sauce.

中华名小吃 Dumplings Plus Flr1/ 269 Swanston St Melbourne 3000

(03) 9663 9898

Categories.value: Thai cuisine in Australia|Flickr images reviewed by FlickreviewR 2|Files from rice tag of Alpha Flickr stream uploaded by Netha Hussain|Kao Gaeng, Springvale

ImageDescription.value:
Thai Fried Rice with Chicken- Kao Gang AUD10.50 --- We initially wanted to try Pawan Thai across the car park, but it was full, so it was back to the reliable Kao Gang, only to find that they were under new management. Still the food was as good as before. There were 2 other Thai families dining while we were there. I guess that means it is quite authentic!

We all loved the Thai dressing on the deep-fried bream. It was intensely sweet, sour, salty and spicy hot! It was thick and syrupy. Perhaps it could have been a little less salty, but it was still good. So salty, we had to order an extra serve of plain steamed rice so that we could soak up the dressing! :P

The grilled Thai sausages were a bit of an eye-opener. It was filled with sour pork and toasted rice. I think the sausage was fermented, giving it a tangy sour taste.

Kao Gang 22-38 Queens Avenue, Springvale (03) 9540 3199
